title: Incline Barbell Bench Press
summary: A barbell press on a 30–45° bench that shifts work toward the upper chest.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates; rack with J-hooks (power rack, squat stands or bench uprights); adjustable (incline) bench.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for chest (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly chest total.
Library rating 0.6 for front delts (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly front delts total.
Library rating 0.5 for triceps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly triceps total.

setup.text: Set the bench at 30–45° and sit with your eyes just in front of the bar.
Pull your shoulder blades back and grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Lower the bar to your upper chest, just below your collarbones.
Press up until your arms are straight over your shoulders.

form_cues.cue: Lower the bar to your upper chest
Keep shoulder blades pinned to the bench
Press straight up over the shoulders
A lower incline (around 30°) keeps more of the work on the chest instead of the shoulders.

mistakes.text: Setting the bench so steep the lift turns into a shoulder press.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Set safety arms or pins where a missed rep can be set down, or use a spotter, and use collars.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.
